ei.title: How a Growing Closedness of Mind Endangers Us with Age
ei.subject: 6월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: How a Growing Closedness of Mind Endangers Us with Age

fullPassage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.

questions.passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became (A)[bored / entranced] by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences (B)[enriched / damaged] our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of (C)[humility / superiority] slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 매료된(entranced) / (B) 풍요롭게 한(enriched) / (C) 우월감(superiority)
det.analysis:
(A) entranced(매료된): 새로운 생각에 '매료되었다'는 흐름이라 entranced가 맞아요. bored(지루한)는 반대예요.

(B) enriched(풍요롭게 한): 그런 영향이 우리의 정신세계를 '풍요롭게 했다'는 뜻이라 enriched가 맞아요. damaged(손상시킨)는 반대예요.

(C) superiority(우월감): 나이 들며 생기는 '우월감'이 마음을 닫게 한다는 흐름이라 superiority가 맞아요. humility(겸손)는 반대예요.

✅① entranced — enriched — superiority가 정답이고, ❌②(bored) ❌③(damaged) ❌④(humility)는 한 자리가 틀려요.
det.tip: 젊을 땐 매료·풍요, 나이 들며 '우월감(superiority)'으로 마음이 닫힘

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 영향(influence) / (B) 지성(intelligence) / (C) 회의적인(skeptical)
det.analysis:
(A) influence(영향): '영향에 매우 열려 있었기에'라는 흐름이라 influence가 맞아요. isolation(고립)은 문맥과 안 맞아요.

(B) intelligence(지성): 우리의 '지성'은 나이 든 이들의 가르침을 흡수하는 능력에 달렸다는 뜻이라 intelligence가 맞아요. ignorance(무지)는 반대예요.

(C) skeptical(회의적인): 현대에 더 '회의적'이 되자고 주장할 수도 있다는 흐름이라 skeptical이 맞아요. gullible(잘 속는)은 반대예요.

✅② influence — intelligence — skeptical이 정답이고, ❌①(isolation) ❌③(ignorance) ❌④(gullible)는 한 자리가 틀려요.
det.tip: 지성(intelligence)은 남의 가르침을 '흡수'하는 능력에 달림

Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing (C)[opening / closing] of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 약함(weakness) / (B) 동기를 부여한(motivated) / (C) 닫힘(closing)
det.analysis:
(A) weakness(약함): '약함과 취약함을 느끼는 감각'이 배움의 욕구를 자극했다는 흐름이라 weakness가 맞아요. strength(강함)는 반대예요.

(B) motivated(동기를 부여한): 그 감각이 배우려는 욕구를 '자극했다'는 뜻이라 motivated가 맞아요. discouraged(의욕을 꺾은)는 반대예요.

(C) closing(닫힘): 더 큰 위험은 마음의 '닫힘'에서 온다는 흐름이라 closing이 맞아요. opening(열림)은 반대예요.

✅③ weakness — motivated — closing이 정답이고, ❌①(strength) ❌②(discouraged) ❌④(opening)는 한 자리가 틀려요.
det.tip: 약함은 배움을 자극, 우월감은 마음의 '닫힘(closing)'을 부름

Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of ③<u>superiority</u> slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ opening → closing: 더 큰 위험은 마음의 '닫힘(closing)'에서 오므로 '열림(opening)'은 부적절
det.analysis:
① entranced(매료된): 새 생각에 매료되었다 — 맞아요.

② enriched(풍요롭게 한): 영향이 정신세계를 풍요롭게 했다 — 맞아요.

③ superiority(우월감): 나이 들며 생기는 우월감 — 맞아요.

④ opening(열림): 원문은 closing이에요. 더 큰 위험은 마음이 점점 '닫히는' 데서 온다는 흐름이라, '열림'은 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답
det.tip: a far greater danger comes from the increasing ___ of the mind → 닫힘(closing)

det.korean: ① drained → enriched: 영향이 정신세계를 '풍요롭게 했다(enriched)'가 맞으므로 '고갈시켰다(drained)'는 부적절

② intelligence(지성): 지성이 흡수 능력에 달렸다 — 맞아요.

③ creeping(서서히 커지는): 서서히 커지는 우월감 — 맞아요.

④ danger(위험): 더 큰 위험 — 맞아요.

det.korean: ② younger → wiser: '더 나이 들고 현명한(older and wiser)' 이들의 가르침이므로 '더 어린(younger)'은 부적절
det.analysis:

③ superiority(우월감): 서서히 커지는 우월감 — 맞아요.

④ burdens(짐 지운다): 우리를 짓누른다 — 맞아요.

det.korean: superiority(우월감) ↔ humility(겸손)
det.analysis:
① humility(겸손): '우월감'의 반대라 정답이에요. ←정답

② honesty(정직): 의미축이 전혀 달라요.

③ loyalty(충성): 관련 없어요.

④ memory(기억): 관련 없어요.
det.tip: superiority(우월감) ↔ humility(겸손)

questions.passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more <u>skeptical</u> in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 skeptical과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: skeptical(회의적인) ↔ trusting(잘 믿는)
det.analysis:
① doubtful(의심하는): skeptical과 비슷한 쪽이라 반대가 아니에요(함정).

② trusting(잘 믿는): '회의적인'의 반대라 정답이에요. ←정답

③ suspicious(의심스러워하는): skeptical과 비슷한 쪽이라 함정이에요.

④ curious(호기심 많은): 의미축이 달라요.
det.tip: skeptical(회의적) ↔ trusting(잘 믿는) — doubtful·suspicious는 비슷한 뜻 함정

questions.passage: (A) We became entranced by the <u>novel</u> ideas in the book, which none of us had ever encountered before. (B) She stayed up all night reading a thrilling <u>novel</u> about a young detective in London.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 novel의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) novel = 새로운(형용사) / (B) novel = (장편) 소설(명사)
det.analysis:
(A) 'the novel ideas in the book(책 속의 novel한 생각들)'에서, 아무도 접한 적 없다는 설명과 함께 쓰여 novel은 '새로운/참신한'이라는 형용사예요.

(B) 'reading a thrilling novel(흥미진진한 novel을 읽으며)'에서 novel은 우리가 읽는 '소설'이라는 명사예요.

따라서 (A) 새로운 — (B) (장편) 소설인 ③번이 정답이에요.

✅③이 정답이고, ❌①②④는 두 문맥 중 하나가 어긋나요.
det.tip: novel: 형용사 '새로운' vs 명사 '소설'

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to publicly support or recommend a particular idea, plan, or way of doing something"

det.korean: 정의 = '어떤 생각·방안을 공개적으로 지지하거나 권하다' → advocate(옹호하다)
det.analysis:
① absorb(흡수하다): 뜻이 달라요.

② enrich(풍요롭게 하다): 관련 없어요.

③ tighten(조이다): 전혀 달라요.

④ advocate(옹호하다/주장하다): '어떤 생각을 공개적으로 지지·권하다'라는 정의와 일치해요. 본문의 advocate와 같은 단어예요. ←정답
det.tip: publicly support an idea = 옹호하다 → advocate

questions.passage: And just as our sense of __________ (weak) and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: weak(형용사, 약한) → weakness(명사, 약함). 'our sense of ___ and vulnerability'에서 of의 목적어인 명사 자리
det.analysis: 빈칸은 'our sense of __________ and vulnerability'로, 전치사 of의 목적어이면서 명사 vulnerability와 and로 이어지는 명사 자리예요. 형용사 weak를 명사형 weakness로 바꿔 '약함'이 돼야 해요.
det.tip: sense of ___ and vulnerability → 명사 weakness

questions.passage: Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our __________ (intelligent) depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: intelligent(형용사, 지적인) → intelligence(명사, 지성). 'our __________ depends on'에서 주어인 명사 자리
det.analysis: 빈칸은 'our __________ depends on the ability'로, 동사 depends의 주어인 명사 자리예요. 형용사 intelligent를 명사형 intelligence로 바꿔 '우리의 지성'이 돼야 해요.
det.tip: our ___ depends on → 주어 명사 intelligence

questions.passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so __________, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: open to influence — '영향에 매우 열려 있었기에' 생각이 깊이 스며듦
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤에 '흥미로운 생각이 마음 깊이 스며들어 사고 과정의 일부가 되었다'가 이어져요. 생각이 깊이 들어오려면 마음이 받아들이는 상태여야 해요.

✅① open to influence(영향에 열린): 영향을 잘 받아들였기에 생각이 깊이 스며든다는 흐름에 맞아요. ←정답

❌② afraid of change(변화를 두려워하는): 받아들임과 반대예요.

❌③ tired of reading(독서에 지친): 책에 매료된 흐름과 모순돼요.

❌④ sure of ourselves(스스로 확신하는): 나이 든 뒤의 우월감에 가까워 젊은 시절과 안 맞아요.
det.tip: 생각이 깊이 스며듦 → 영향에 '열려(open to influence)' 있었음

questions.passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from __________ that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: the increasing closing of the mind — 나이 들수록 커지는 '마음의 닫힘'이 더 큰 위험
det.analysis:
글은 젊을 땐 영향에 열려 배우지만, 나이 들며 우월감이 생겨 새 생각에 마음을 닫는다고 해요. 빈칸은 '더 큰 위험은 ___에서 온다'예요.

✅② the increasing closing of the mind(점점 심해지는 마음의 닫힘): 바로 앞에서 우월감이 '마음을 닫게 한다'고 했으니 정답이에요. ←정답

❌① the high dependence on others(타인에 대한 큰 의존): 본문에 없어요.

❌③ the obsession with our inferiority(열등감에 대한 집착): 본문은 '우월감'을 말하니 반대예요.

❌④ the misconception about our psychology(우리 심리에 대한 오해): 언급이 없어요.
det.tip: 우월감이 마음을 닫음 → the increasing closing of the mind
